This plot is small, only a quarter hectare, but maize is what feeds my family so I must treat it well. I will buy some fertilizer if I can — maybe through the subsidy if I am lucky — but the price is high so I cannot put as much as they tell us at the extension office. I keep a few chickens and goats, so I will carry their manure to the field before planting, and I will buy improved seed from the shop in town because the yield is better than the seed I save. I cannot irrigate here, we wait for the rains, and most of the work my wife and I will do ourselves, hiring only a few people for weeding if the weeds get ahead of us.
